deviations.what: handleCalendarSelect/_updateText read the picked day off the control (oCalendar.getSelectedDates()[0].getStartDate()) and format it yyyy-MM-dd. The port transports it as three UI5 expression args (year, month+1, day - the LOCAL parts, not toISOString( ), which would shift the day east of Greenwich), each guarded by getSelectedDates().length > 0, and formats server-side; the Text gets a two-way bound text attribute instead of setText (app 139 idiom, probe-verified). The controller's oLastSelectedJSDate becomes a server-side field, so the second click on the same day is recognised exactly as in the original.

handleCalendarSelect's oCalendar.removeSelectedDate(oSelectedDate) is reproduced since 2026-08-21: the second click on the same day sends a control_by_id follow-up action calling removeAllSelectedDates on the calendar, so the day loses its highlight the way it does in the original. This carried an IMPROVISED deviation until then, on the claim that removeSelectedDate takes a DateRange CONTROL instance no wire can address - true of that method, but the calendar is single-selection (the view sets neither singleSelection nor intervalSelection), so at most one DateRange exists and removeAllSelectedDates removes exactly it. abap2UI5 #2535 un-denied that method for this reason and the sibling port 307 has been calling it 1:1 since; 305's copy of the deviation had simply outlived it.

onInit does byId('calendar').displayDate(UI5Date.getInstance(2021, 6, 1)) to open the calendar on July 2021, and the port opens on the current month instead. Two of the three reasons this note used to give are wrong and are corrected here. displayDate( ) itself is indeed unreachable: it takes a JS Date and the frontend-action wire casts only string/int/bool/controlId/controlIdOrNull/within/object/anchor kinds. But "Calendar exposes no bindable property for the displayed month" is FALSE - sap.ui.unified.Calendar.initialFocusedDate (@since 1.111) is exactly that property - and "a JS Date abap2UI5 cannot hold" is false too: it is typed object like minDate/maxDate, and app 220 feeds those on this very control from an ABAP DATS string through the curated Formatter.DateAbapDateToDateObject, which is new Date(...parseYmd(d)) - the same local-parts Date the original builds. MEASURED 2026-08-26 in the e2e browser (a probe swapped into this port's interaction module and restored): a Calendar constructed with initialFocusedDate opens on July 2021, and the month survives header navigation and a selection. What blocks the port is the third fact, which no version or wire question would have surfaced: initialFocusedDate is not a one-shot like displayDate( ) - Calendar.onBeforeRendering re-applies it on EVERY render (this._oFocusedDate = CalendarDate.fromLocalJSDate(this.getInitialFocusedDate(), ...)), and the probe confirmed a full invalidate( ) snaps the calendar back to July 2021. This app's second-click branch calls removeAllSelectedDates on the calendar, which invalidates it, so binding the property would trade a wrong start month for a calendar that jumps back to July whenever a day is deselected. Left unported deliberately, with the obstacle now named correctly.
Calendar.showCurrentDateButton (@since 1.95) is kept 1:1 from the original view. Newer than UI5 1.71.

The sample's own stylesheet is injected since 2026-08-21 through an added core:HTML style leaf (no counterpart in the original view). This sample's manifest lists `../style.css` - the sheet the sap.ui.unified samples SHARE one folder up - and it was never archived, so the viewPadding / labelMarginLeft classes the view carries had no rule behind them and the port rendered flush against the page edge where the sample renders padded. The sheet now sits at ui5/sap.ui.unified/style.css (closing the AGENTS section 4 archive gap) and only the rules this view actually uses are injected. Found by scripts/probes/orphan-style-class-probe.mjs. Corrected 2026-08-23: the sheet's .sap-phone .sapUiCal{position:relative} rule was dropped as "not used by the view" and is injected now - sapUiCal is written by CalendarRenderer on the Calendar's own root, not by the author, so it does reach this view on a phone. Same sweep as apps 139/177/220/240/305/306/307/308. The sheet's remaining rule targets .sapUiCancel, which no OpenUI5 renderer writes.
